title: Hey, Ḍombī
voice: Kāṇha, a kāpālika yogi, sings straight at Ḍombī at her hut outside the town: teasing, courting, showing off his outcaste gear, then turning without warning to the threat. A border ballad's bluntness.
refrainCue: Hey Ḍombī, I'll keep company with you

lines.en: Out past the town, Ḍombī, stands your hut;
the brahmin goes by, touching, touching, his head close-cut.
Hey Ḍombī, I'll keep company with you:
Kāṇha, kāpālika yogi, without disgust, clings to you.
A single lotus with sixty-four petals:
poor Ḍombī climbs up on it and dances.
Hey Ḍombī, I ask in good faith, I want to know:
in whose boat, Ḍombī, do you come and go?
Ḍombī sells cord now, and no more baskets;
for your sake I've put down the performer's basket.
Hey you, Ḍombī, I am a kāpālika;
for your sake I've put on a garland of bones.
Breaking the lake, Ḍombī eats the lotus root.
I'll kill Ḍombī. I'll take her life.

couplets.kept: Perfect rhyme on hut / close-cut for kuṛiā / nāṛiā; the doubled 'touching, touching' kept as the source doubles chaichoi.
Absolute rhyme, you / you, for the refrain the song keeps coming back to; Ḍombī named at its start.
couplets.letGo: The vowel rhyme of sāṅga / lāga.

couplets.kept: The one lotus, its sixty-four petals, and poor Ḍombī dancing on it, plainly.
couplets.letGo: The perfect rhyme of pākhuṛī / bāpuṛī: nothing honest rhymes with petals.

couplets.kept: Perfect rhyme on know / go for sadabhābe / nābem̐, and Ḍombī called twice, as in the source.
couplets.letGo: 'I want to know' spells out what the asking implies.

couplets.kept: Baskets / basket keeps the same word at both ends, a rougher chime than the source's off rhyme.
couplets.letGo: The gloss is unsure of both baskets; the version does not say so.

couplets.kept: The boast and the garland of bones, short and hard.
couplets.letGo: The perfect rhyme of kapālī / mālī.

couplets.kept: The turn to the threat, as sudden as the source's; both last lines end on a stress, like a door slammed.
couplets.letGo: The perfect rhyme of molāṇa / parāṇa.

note: An example made with Claude to show the ballad lens; unreviewed.
